- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.1) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent 5-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag sentiment shifts; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough.
